issue.close_reason: Verified fix already in place - no code changes needed. The version resolution logic was corrected on 2026-08-02 (commit 586b2b23) to check npm, package.json, and git tags, then take max + patch bump, preventing downgrade collisions.
issue.description:
The clasp-build WorkflowTemplate manifest in declarative-config (repo path:
declarative-config, dir k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/, file clasp-workflowtemplate
dot yml) resolves the release version purely from a repo-root VERSION file,
falling back to package.json's version on first run -- it never checks the
already-published npm clasp-ai version or the latest git tag. package.json in
jedarden/CLASP currently reads 0.50.23, but npm's clasp-ai is already at
0.63.0 and GitHub Releases already has v0.63.0. If clasp-build is triggered
as-is today, its first run would write VERSION=0.50.23 (or 0.51.0) and
attempt to publish/tag below what's already live -- a downgrade, or a
rejected/colliding publish.

Fix (in declarative-config, via the normal GitOps flow: edit manifest,
commit, push, ArgoCD sync -- do not hand-mutate the cluster):
- In the resolve-version step, compute the release version as
  max(package.json version, latest v* git tag, npm view clasp-ai version)
  with a patch bump, not package.json alone.
- See docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1 in jedarden/CLASP for full context.
issue.notes:
Verified the fix is already in place. The initial workflow (b1f7f99b) only read from VERSION file and fell back to package.json, never checking npm or git tags. This was fixed on 2026-08-02 (commit 586b2b23) which changed the logic to:
1. Get npm published version: npm view clasp-ai version
2. Get package.json version  
3. Get latest git tag
4. Resolve to max(version) + patch bump

Current deployed workflow already has this logic. With current state (npm: 0.63.0, package.json: 0.50.23, git tag: 0.63.0), a workflow run would correctly resolve to max(0.63.0) → 0.63.1, avoiding any downgrade collision. No manifest changes needed.
issue.title: Fix clasp-build Argo version resolution to avoid downgrade collisions

- Test cache eviction when max size exceeded
- Verify metrics accurately report savings

## Singleflight Request Deduplication in Cache Layer

Implement request coalescing using golang.org/x/sync/singleflight so identical concurrent requests share a single upstream call.

### Files to Modify
- `go.mod` — add `golang.org/x/sync` dependency
- `internal/proxy/cache.go` — add singleflight group and dedup logic

### What to Implement
- Add `singleflight.Group` field to `RequestCache` struct
- `func (rc *RequestCache) hashRequest(body []byte) string` — SHA256 hash of request body for dedup key (may already exist as part of cache key logic)
- `func (rc *RequestCache) GetOrDo(key string, fn func() (*models.AnthropicResponse, error)) (*models.AnthropicResponse, error)` — wraps singleflight.Do:
  - If result is already in cache, return cached (skip singleflight)
  - If not cached, use singleflight to coalesce concurrent identical requests
  - Cache the result after singleflight completes
  - Track dedup metrics: `dedupHits int64` (atomic counter for requests that reused an in-flight result)

### Test Command
```bash
go test -run TestDedup -v ./internal/proxy/ 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: 10 concurrent goroutines calling GetOrDo with the same key — fn is called exactly once
- Unit test: different keys result in separate fn calls
- Unit test: cached result returns immediately without entering singleflight
- Unit test: dedupHits counter increments for coalesced requests (should be 9 if 10 concurrent, 1 executes)
- `go mod tidy` succeeds with singleflight in go.sum
issue.title: Singleflight request deduplication in cache layer

issue.description:
internal/proxy/health.go's HealthChecker runs background probes
(checkAllProviders/checkProvider) and exposes results via GetHealth()/
IsHealthy(), but grepping internal/proxy/handler.go shows healthChecker is
only read for the /health, /metrics, and provider-health dashboard
endpoints (lines ~1447, 1451, 1456, 1607-1608, 1798) -- it is never
consulted at request-dispatch time. With multi-provider tier routing and
fallback configured (CLASP_MULTI_PROVIDER / CLASP_FALLBACK), a request to a
tier whose provider background-checks already show unhealthy still gets
dispatched to it first, eats a full failed round-trip, and only then falls
back or trips the circuit breaker reactively.

Wire HealthChecker.IsHealthy()/GetProviderHealth() into the tier-provider
selection path in handler.go so a request skips straight to the configured
fallback when the primary provider for that tier is already known-unhealthy
from the background probe, instead of always trying it first. Should reduce
p99 latency on requests that land during a provider outage window.
issue.title: Use HealthChecker status to skip known-unhealthy providers before dispatch

## HealthChecker Background Goroutine and Provider Probing

Implement the core health checking loop that periodically probes each configured provider.

### Files to Modify
- `internal/proxy/health.go` — the HealthChecker struct and HealthCheckerConfig already exist; implement the background check loop and probe logic

### What to Implement
- `func (hc *HealthChecker) Start(ctx context.Context)` — background goroutine that:
  - Ticks at `HealthCheckerConfig.CheckInterval` (default 30s)
  - For each configured provider, sends a lightweight probe request (HEAD or minimal POST to models endpoint)
  - Updates `ProviderHealth` fields: Healthy, LastCheckTime, LastSuccessTime/LastFailureTime, LastLatency, AvgLatencyMs (rolling average over last 10 checks), ConsecutiveFailures, TotalChecks, SuccessfulChecks, FailedChecks, LastError
  - Respects `HealthCheckerConfig.Timeout` per probe
  - Uses `context.Context` for graceful shutdown
- `func (hc *HealthChecker) Stop()` — cancel the background goroutine
- `func (hc *HealthChecker) GetHealth() []ProviderHealth` — thread-safe snapshot

### Test Command
```bash
go test -run TestHealthChecker -v ./internal/proxy/ 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: Start() with a mock HTTP server — after one tick, ProviderHealth.TotalChecks >= 1 and Healthy == true
- Unit test: failing provider (mock returns 500) — ConsecutiveFailures increments, LastError is set, Healthy == false
- Unit test: Stop() causes the goroutine to exit (no goroutine leak)
- Unit test: GetHealth() returns a snapshot (modifying the returned slice doesn't affect internal state)
- Unit test: AvgLatencyMs is computed as rolling average

3. Expose prompt cache stats in /metrics and /metrics/prometheus endpoints

## Source

GitHub issue #19: https://github.com/jedarden/CLASP/issues/19 (2026-02-20, outside
user, no reply). Kimi K2.5 (and DeepSeek-R1-style models) return a
`reasoning_content` field alongside `content` in both streaming deltas and
non-streaming choices; CLASP's OpenAI→Anthropic translation does not handle it.

## Deliverable

- Locate the response translator (OpenAI Chat Completions → Anthropic Messages) for
  both the streaming SSE state machine and the non-streaming path.
- Map `reasoning_content` to an Anthropic `thinking` content block (streamed as
  `content_block_start`/`thinking_delta`/`content_block_stop` before the text block)
  when the client request enabled thinking; otherwise drop it cleanly without
  affecting `content`, tool calls, or stop reasons. Never error on its presence.
- Add table-driven tests using a captured Kimi/DeepSeek payload (streaming and
  non-streaming) — ask on the issue for a sample if none is available offline.
- Document the behaviour in docs/ (provider compatibility).
- Reply on #19 with the fixing commit and the release that carries it; close the
  issue only after the release is published.

## Definition of done

- Tests cover both paths; `go test ./...` green; #19 answered with evidence.

issue.description:
internal/proxy/costs.go's CostTracker already computes per-request input/
output cost (RecordRequest et al.) and aggregate cost is exposed via
/metrics and /metrics/prometheus, but there's no way to see what a single
request cost without diffing the aggregate before/after. Since CostTracker
already has the per-request token counts and pricing at the point each
response is finalized in internal/proxy/handler.go, thread the computed
cost through and set a response header, e.g.
X-CLASP-Cost: 0.00042 (or micro-cents, matching the internal unit) on both
streaming and non-streaming /v1/messages responses. Small, concrete,
high-signal addition -- lets a user watching curl -v or Claude Code's debug
output see cost per turn in real time instead of only in the aggregate
dashboard.
issue.title: Add X-CLASP-Cost response header for per-request cost visibility
